fullPassage:
Hello, first-year students. I'm your school counselor, Hannah Kim. How is your new school life? You may have experienced a situation where things didn't go as you expected at school. Have you ever wondered why this happens? Let's take a look at the following two cases.

The first case is about a student named Hajun. On the first day of school, Hajun's homeroom teacher introduced several school clubs. At that time, Hajun didn't have a particular preference for any of them. He thought that any indoor club would be okay since he was not an outdoor person. Can you guess what happened on the day of choice? He joined the soccer club. What made him choose soccer?

Well, a few days before submitting his application, he heard that the soccer club was so popular that half of his classmates were applying for it. This made him think that the soccer club was something special. With this in mind, he signed up for the soccer club just because others did so. However, after he had joined the club, he realized that soccer was not for him. In the end, he regretted his decision.

Why do you think this happened? Psychologists say that people tend to engage in certain behaviors just because others are doing them. Also, people don't want to be excluded from their peers. These psychological factors cause people to follow the crowd, rather than act on their own. This phenomenon is called the "bandwagon effect." Following the crowd, of course, does not always lead to negative consequences, but it can lead to regret. So, how can you make your own choices? The first thing is to know what you really want. Although it might be different from your friends', don't be afraid to make your own choice. As long as you make the right choice for you, you will be happy about your decision.

Now, let's look at another case, one about Yubin. One day, Yubin told me about her first science quiz. Science was the subject that she struggled with the most. Since she wanted to get a good grade, she made a thorough study plan for herself. Yet, every time she tried to concentrate on science, she found herself doing other things instead. For instance, she cleaned her desk or texted her friends. These activities distracted her from studying, and in the end, she got a bad grade. She was frustrated that she continuously engaged in behaviors unhelpful for accomplishing her task.

When people do not have the confidence to perform tasks well, they are likely to create obstacles to success. This type of behavior is referred to as "self-handicapping." Self-handicapping enables people to make excuses for their poor performances. These excuses prevent the poor result from lowering their self-esteem. This might work in the short term. However, be careful! It could lead to repeated failures in certain tasks that you are not confident in doing.

If you are self-handicapping, it might be because you consider the results more important than the process. Focusing more on the process than the outcome may ease the pressure to perform well. Accordingly, you may feel more encouraged to try to do the challenging tasks. This can eventually stop your self-handicapping.

As first-year students in high school, you'll sometimes face difficult moments. It is not unusual because everyone goes through difficult times. Even though you feel disappointed with your choices or behaviors, don't let yourself feel down. The most important thing is figuring out your own way to overcome your negative feelings. It will make your school life much more enjoyable. If you feel worried, remember that you are not alone. You have friends, teachers, and me. Good luck in this exciting new chapter of your life.

questions.passage: Well, a few days before ①<u>submitting</u> his application, he heard that the soccer club was so popular that half of his classmates ②<u>was</u> applying for it. This made him ③<u>think</u> that the soccer club was something special. With this in mind, he signed up for the soccer club just because others ④<u>did</u> so.
questions.stem: 위 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: 지원서를 제출하기 며칠 전, 반 친구 절반이 지원하고 있다는 것을 들었다. 이것은 그가 축구 동아리가 특별하다고 생각하게 만들었다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① submitting: before + 동명사. 정상.
❌ ② was → were: 주어가 half of his classmates(복수)이므로 were가 맞음.
✅ ③ think: made him think (사역동사 + 목적어 + 동사원형). 정상.
✅ ④ did: did so = signed up (대동사). 정상.
det.tip: half of + 복수명사 → 복수 동사 / make + O + 동사원형: ~하게 만들다

questions.passage: However, after he had ①<u>joined</u> the club, he realized that soccer was not for him. In the end, he regretted his decision. Psychologists say that people tend to ②<u>engage</u> in certain behaviors just because others are doing them. Also, people don't want to be ③<u>excluding</u> from their peers. These psychological factors cause people ④<u>to follow</u> the crowd.
questions.stem: 위 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: 동아리에 가입한 후 축구가 자신에게 맞지 않다는 것을 깨달았다. 사람들은 또래에게서 배제되는 것을 원하지 않는다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① joined: 과거완료(had joined). 정상.
✅ ② engage: tend to engage (to부정사 + 동사원형). 정상.
❌ ③ excluding → excluded: 수동태 필요. '배제되다(be excluded)'. excluding은 능동 의미.
✅ ④ to follow: cause people to follow (cause + O + to-V). 정상.
det.tip: be excluded from: ~에서 배제되다 (수동) / excluding(능동: 배제하는) vs excluded(수동: 배제되는)

questions.passage: When people do not have the confidence to perform tasks well, they are likely to create obstacles to success. This type of behavior is ①<u>referred</u> to as "self-handicapping." Self-handicapping enables people ②<u>to make</u> excuses for their poor performances. These excuses prevent the poor result from ③<u>lower</u> their self-esteem. This might work in the ④<u>short</u> term.
questions.stem: 위 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: 자신감이 없을 때 성공에 대한 장애물을 만든다. 이 변명들은 저조한 결과가 자존감을 낮추는 것을 막는다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① referred: is referred to as (수동태). 정상.
✅ ② to make: enables people to make (enable + O + to-V). 정상.
❌ ③ lower → lowering: prevent A from ~ing 구문. from 뒤에 동명사 필요.
✅ ④ short: in the short term(단기적으로). 형용사 정상.
det.tip: prevent A from ~ing: A가 ~하는 것을 막다 / enable A to-V: A가 ~할 수 있게 하다

questions.passage: If you are self-handicapping, it might be because you consider the results more important than the process. ①<u>Focusing</u> more on the process than the outcome may ease the pressure to perform well. Accordingly, you may feel more ②<u>encouraging</u> to try to do the challenging tasks. This can ③<u>eventually</u> stop your self-handicapping. det.korean: 과정에 더 집중하면 압박감을 줄일 수 있다. 따라서 도전적인 과제를 시도하려는 마음이 더 들 수 있다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① Focusing: 동명사 주어. 정상.
❌ ② encouraging → encouraged: 감정의 주체(you)가 '격려받는' 느낌이므로 과거분사 encouraged. encouraging은 '격려하는(감정 유발)'.
✅ ③ eventually: 부사, 동사 stop 수식. 정상.
✅ ④ face: will face(미래시제 동사원형). 정상.
det.tip: encouraged(격려받은, 감정 주체) vs encouraging(격려하는, 감정 원인) / -ed vs -ing 분사형용사

questions.stem: 위 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중, 문맥상 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: 하준의 담임이 동아리를 소개했다. 하준은 특별한 선호가 없었다. 축구 동아리가 인기 있다는 말을 듣고 ④<u>평범한</u> 것이라고 생각했다.
det.analysis:
✅ ①②③ 원문 그대로 적절.
❌ ④ ordinary(평범한) → 원문은 special(특별한). 반 친구 절반이 지원할 정도로 인기가 있어서 '특별한' 것이라 생각한 문맥. ordinary는 반대.
det.tip: special(특별한) ↔ ordinary(평범한) / preference: 선호 / application: 지원서

questions.passage: Yet, every time she tried to concentrate on science, she found herself doing other things instead. For instance, she cleaned her desk or texted her friends. These activities ①<u>distracted</u> her from studying, and in the end, she got a bad grade. She was ②<u>frustrated</u> that she continuously engaged in behaviors unhelpful for ③<u>accomplishing</u> her task. When people do not have the confidence to perform tasks well, they are likely to create ④<u>shortcuts</u> to success.
questions.stem: 위 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중, 문맥상 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: 이 활동들은 공부에서 주의를 ①분산시켰고, 결국 나쁜 성적을 받았다. 그녀는 과제 ③완수에 도움이 되지 않는 행동을 계속한 것에 ②좌절했다. 자신감이 없으면 성공에 대한 ④지름길을 만든다.
det.analysis:
✅ ①②③ 원문 그대로 적절.
❌ ④ shortcuts(지름길) → 원문은 obstacles(장애물). 자신감이 없을 때 성공에 대한 '장애물'을 만드는 것이 자기 핸디캡핑. shortcuts는 정반대 의미.
det.tip: obstacles(장애물) ↔ shortcuts(지름길) / distract A from B: A를 B에서 주의를 분산시키다

questions.passage: At that time, Hajun didn't have a particular preference for any of them. He thought that any indoor club would be okay since he was not an outdoor person. Can you guess what happened on the day of choice? He joined the soccer club.
questions.stem:
위 글의 내용으로 보아 다음 진술이 맞으면 T, 틀리면 F를 고르시오.
"하준은 처음부터 축구 동아리에 대한 강한 선호가 있었다."

det.korean: 하준은 어느 동아리에도 특별한 선호가 없었다. 실내 동아리면 괜찮다고 생각했을 뿐이다.
det.analysis: ✅ F: 원문에서 'didn't have a particular preference for any of them'이라고 명시. 강한 선호가 있었다는 것은 거짓.
det.tip: particular preference: 특별한 선호 / didn't have: 가지고 있지 않았다

questions.passage: Self-handicapping enables people to make excuses for their poor performances. These excuses prevent the poor result from lowering their self-esteem. This might work in the short term.
questions.stem:
위 글의 내용으로 보아 다음 진술이 맞으면 T, 틀리면 F를 고르시오.
"자기 핸디캡핑의 변명은 단기적으로 자존감을 보호하는 효과가 있을 수 있다."

det.korean: 변명이 저조한 결과가 자존감을 낮추는 것을 막는다. 이것은 단기적으로 효과가 있을 수 있다.
det.analysis: ✅ T: excuses prevent poor result from lowering self-esteem + might work in the short term. 진술과 일치.
det.tip: self-esteem: 자존감 / in the short term: 단기적으로 / prevent from ~ing: ~하는 것을 막다

det.analysis: ✅ T: 원문과 정확히 일치. figuring out your own way to overcome negative feelings → make school life more enjoyable.
det.tip: figure out: 알아내다 / overcome: 극복하다 / enjoyable: 즐거운

questions.passage: Well, a few days before submitting his application, he heard that the soccer club was so popular that half of his classmates were applying for it. This made him think that the soccer club was something special. With this in mind, he signed up for the soccer club just because others did so. However, after he had joined the club, he realized that soccer was not for him. In the end, he __________ his decision.
questions.stem: 위 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 축구가 자신에게 맞지 않다는 것을 깨달은 후, 결국 그는 자신의 결정을 후회했다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② regretted: 축구가 자신에게 맞지 않다는 것을 깨달았으므로 결정을 '후회'.
❌ ① celebrated(축하했다): 맞지 않다는 깨달음 후 축하는 부적합.
❌ ③ defended(옹호했다): 후회할 상황에서 옹호는 부적합.
❌ ④ postponed(연기했다): 이미 가입한 후이므로 연기 불가.
det.tip: regret one's decision: 결정을 후회하다 / realize: 깨닫다 / not for him: 그에게 맞지 않는

questions.passage: When people do not have the confidence to perform tasks well, they are likely to create obstacles to success. This type of behavior is referred to as "self-handicapping." Self-handicapping enables people to make excuses for their poor performances. These excuses prevent the poor result from lowering their self-esteem. This might work in the short term. However, be careful! It could lead to __________ in certain tasks that you are not confident in doing.
questions.stem: 위 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 단기적으로 효과가 있을 수 있지만, 주의하라! 자신 없는 과제에서 반복되는 실패로 이어질 수 있다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② repeated failures: However, be careful! 뒤에 부정적 결과 제시. 자신 없는 과제에서 '반복 실패'.
❌ ① unexpected success: 경고 뒤에 성공은 문맥 모순.
❌ ③ instant recovery: 즉각적 회복은 경고와 모순.
❌ ④ steady progress: 꾸준한 발전은 경고와 모순.
det.tip: repeated failures: 반복되는 실패 / However, be careful!: 경고 → 부정적 결과 예고

questions.passage: Now, let's look at another case, one about Yubin. One day, Yubin told me about her first science quiz. Science was the subject that she struggled with the most. Since she wanted to get a good grade, she made a thorough study plan for herself. Yet, every time she tried to concentrate on science, she found herself doing other things instead.
questions.stem: 위 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
ch: ① 유빈은 과학이 가장 자신 있는 과목이었다.
② 유빈은 학습 계획을 세우지 않았다.
③ 유빈은 과학에 집중하려 할 때마다 다른 일을 하게 되었다.
④ 유빈은 첫 과학 시험에서 좋은 성적을 받았다.

det.korean: 유빈은 과학이 가장 힘든 과목이었다. 좋은 성적을 원해서 계획을 세웠지만, 집중하려 할 때마다 다른 일을 하게 되었다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ 원문과 일치: every time she tried to concentrate on science, she found herself doing other things instead.
❌ ① 가장 자신 있는 → 원문은 struggled with the most(가장 힘든).
❌ ② 계획 안 세움 → 원문은 made a thorough study plan.
❌ ④ 좋은 성적 → 원문은 got a bad grade.
det.tip: struggle with: ~를 힘들어하다 / concentrate on: ~에 집중하다 / find oneself ~ing: 자신이 ~하고 있음을 알다

questions.passage: Psychologists say that people tend to engage in certain behaviors just because others are doing them. Also, people don't want to be excluded from their peers. These psychological factors cause people to follow the crowd, rather than act on their own. This phenomenon is called the "bandwagon effect." Following the crowd, of course, does not always lead to negative consequences, but it can lead to regret.
questions.stem: 위 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
ch: ① 사람들은 다른 사람이 한다는 이유로 특정 행동에 참여하는 경향이 있다.
② 사람들은 또래에게서 배제되고 싶어 하지 않는다.
③ 이 현상은 편승 효과라고 불린다.
④ 군중을 따르는 것은 항상 부정적 결과로 이어진다.

det.korean: 군중을 따르는 것이 '항상' 부정적 결과를 초래하는 것은 아니지만, 후회로 이어질 수 있다.
det.analysis:
✅ ①②③ 원문과 일치.
❌ ④ '항상 부정적 결과' → 원문은 'does not always lead to negative consequences'. '항상'이 아니라는 부분이 핵심 차이.
det.tip: not always: 항상 ~은 아니다 (부분 부정) / consequence: 결과

questions.passage: ①The first thing is to know what you really want. ②Although it might be different from your friends', don't be afraid to make your own choice. ③As long as you make the right choice for you, you will be happy about your decision. ④Focusing more on the outcome than the process may ease the pressure to perform well.
questions.stem: 위 글의 ①~④ 중 원문의 내용과 다른 문장은?

det.korean: ①진정으로 원하는 것을 아는 것이 첫째이다. ②친구들과 다르더라도 자신의 선택을 두려워하지 마라. ③올바른 선택을 하면 행복할 것이다. ④결과보다 과정에 집중하면 압박감이 줄어든다.
det.analysis:
✅ ①②③ 원문 그대로.
❌ ④ outcome → process: 원문은 'Focusing more on the process than the outcome'. 과정(process)에 더 집중하라는 것이지, 결과(outcome)에 집중하라는 것이 아님. 순서가 바뀜.
det.tip: 원문: process > outcome (과정 중시) / 오류: outcome > process (결과 중시) — 핵심 단어 순서 뒤바뀜

[the / on / more / process / the / focusing / outcome / ease / than / may / pressure / the / well / to / perform]
(대소문자 구분 없음, 마침표 생략 가능)
questions.wa: Focusing more on the process than the outcome may ease the pressure to perform well

questions.passage: Psychologists say that people tend to engage in certain behaviors just because others are doing them. Also, people don't want to be excluded from their peers. These psychological factors cause people to follow the crowd, rather than act on their own. This phenomenon is called the "bandwagon effect." Following the crowd, of course, does not always lead to negative consequences, but it can lead to regret.
questions.stem: 위 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 다수가 하니까 따라하는 심리적 요인들과 이로 인한 편승 효과, 그리고 후회 가능성.
det.analysis:
✅ ① 편승 효과의 원인(심리적 요인)과 결과(후회 가능성).
❌ ② 의사소통: 언급 없음.
❌ ③ 동아리 선택 기준: 하준의 사례는 예시일 뿐, 주제가 아님.
❌ ④ 자존감 향상: 이 단락의 주제가 아님(자기 핸디캡핑 단락 주제).
det.tip: 글의 주제: 심리적 요인 → 군중 추종(편승 효과) → 후회 가능성

questions.passage: When people do not have the confidence to perform tasks well, they are likely to create obstacles to success. This type of behavior is referred to as "self-handicapping." Self-handicapping enables people to make excuses for their poor performances. If you are self-handicapping, it might be because you consider the results more important than the process. Focusing more on the process than the outcome may ease the pressure to perform well.
questions.stem: 위 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: ① 자신감이 부족하면 스스로 성공의 장애물을 만들지만, 과정에 집중하면 이를 극복할 수 있다.
② 결과만 중시하면 항상 성공할 수 있다.
③ 변명을 많이 하면 자존감이 높아진다.
④ 실패를 반복하는 것이 성장의 유일한 방법이다.

det.korean: 자신감이 없으면 장애물을 만들고(자기 핸디캡핑), 이는 결과를 중시하기 때문. 과정에 집중하면 압박감이 줄어 자기 핸디캡핑을 멈출 수 있다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① 핵심 요약: 자신감 부족 → 장애물(자기 핸디캡핑) + 해결책(과정 집중).
❌ ② 결과 중시로 성공: 원문은 과정 중시를 권장.
❌ ③ 변명으로 자존감 상승: 단기적 보호일 뿐, 반복 실패 경고.
❌ ④ 실패 반복이 유일한 방법: 원문은 실패 반복을 경고.
det.tip: self-handicapping의 원인(결과 중시)과 해결책(과정 집중)이 글의 핵심
